subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Observers: Estimating What You Can't Measure
description: A 60-second lesson on Observers: Estimating What You Can't Measure.

hook.text: Some states can't be measured directly. An observer estimates them from available sensor data.

buildup.text: A Luenberger observer runs a model of the system in parallel and corrects it using measured outputs.

discovery.text: The observer's correction gain determines how fast its estimates converge to the true states.

twist.text: The Kalman filter is the optimal observer for noisy measurements — it minimizes estimation error variance.

climax.text: GPS navigation, drone flight, and spacecraft docking all rely on Kalman filter state estimation.

punchline.text: Can't measure it? Estimate it — observers fill the gaps sensors leave behind.

quiz.question: What makes the Kalman filter 'optimal' as an observer?
options: It uses the least number of calculations
It minimizes the variance of the estimation error given noisy measurements
It requires no model of the system to operate
